intelligence.essence: Every page opens on its optimized viewpoint — one screen, ten-star, alive. Two plus buttons reach your world, settings tucks beneath, fullscreen sits just under. The gauge shows points, percent, and one day one-to-ten.
intelligence.human_view: Shawn's ruling 2026-11-03, on seeing the restored Bugatti dashboard: the fullscreen optimized viewpoint becomes the STANDARD page chrome across NayaNET. Layout order: twin plus buttons (quick tabs to the main areas within the page) → settings underneath the plus → fullscreen button just under that. Bottom or top nav remains as alternate access but can hide — the main screen stays focused, the inner screen, the ten-star screen. The gauge carries output toggles: PTS / % today, a 1-to-10 scale coming (so you can measure whether something's a ten).
intelligence.simple_view: Every page in NayaNET opens looking its best, arranged the same friendly way: two big plus buttons to reach your things, the settings tucked just below, and a fullscreen button right under that — so every page feels like home the moment it opens.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, every room in this house is arranged the same sensible way: the two big buttons where you can always reach them, the settings tucked neatly underneath, the fullscreen button just below. You learn one room and you know every room — no hunting around in a new place.
intelligence.naya_view: I build every page on the standard chrome: optimized viewpoint first (SN-0858 as standard, not principle), twin plus buttons as quick tabs, settings beneath the plus, fullscreen just under, nav present but allowed to hide so the ten-star inner screen stays the focus. The gauge's output toggles — PTS / % today, 1-to-10 coming — ride the same standard.
intelligence.ai_view: One chrome language everywhere means a citizen never re-learns a page. The optimized viewpoint is the Viewport Law (SN-0858) made standard: what is the intent, what is the essence, what can fade — answered the same way on every screen. The page presents NayaNET as a living machine, living intelligence, a smart factory — alive, not a document.
